title_en: Suzhou Industrial Park Haifu Investment Co., Ltd. v. Gansu Shiheng Nonferrous Resources Recycling Co., Ltd., Hong Kong Diya Co., Ltd., and Lu Bo — dispute over capital increase
ruling_gist_en: In private financing and investment activities, the financing party and investors establishing a valuation adjustment mechanism (i.e., the mechanism whereby investors and the financing party adjust investment conditions or provide compensation to investors based on the future operation of the enterprise) must comply with the provisions of the Company Law and the Contract Law. If a compensation clause between the investor and the target company itself allows the investor to obtain a relatively fixed return, such return would be detached from the target company's operating performance and directly or indirectly harm the interests of the company and its creditors; therefore, it should be deemed invalid. However, a compensation commitment made by the shareholders of the target company to the investor, which does not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations, is valid. When the compensation conditions stipulated in the contract are met, based on the principles of party autonomy and good faith, the capital-raising party should honor its promise, and the investor is entitled to the agreed compensation.

full_text_en:
Suzhou Industrial Park Haifu Investment Co., Ltd. v.
Gansu Shiheng Nonferrous Resources Reuse Co., Ltd.,
Hong Kong Diya Co., Ltd., and Lu Bo
— dispute over capital increase

Ruling Summary

In private financing and investment activities, when the financing party and the investor establish a valuation adjustment mechanism (i.e., the investor and the financing party adjust the investment conditions or provide compensation to the investor based on the future business performance of the enterprise), the provisions of the Company Law and the Contract Law must be observed. If a compensation clause between the investor and the target company itself enables the investor to obtain relatively fixed returns, such returns would be detached from the target company's business performance, directly or indirectly harming the interests of the company and its creditors, and therefore should be held invalid. However, a compensation commitment made by the target company's shareholders to the investor does not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations and is valid. Where the conditions for compensation stipulated in the contract are satisfied, the party introducing the investment shall abide by its promise in accordance with the principles of party autonomy and good faith, and the investor is entitled to the agreed compensation.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2012) Min Ti Zi No. 11

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Gansu Shiheng Nonferrous Resources Reuse Co., Ltd. Domicile: Youyi Village, Fengxiang Town, Anding District, Dingxi City, Gansu Province.
Legal Representative: Lu Bo, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Sun Geng, lawyer of Gansu Dehe Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Hong Kong Diya Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 705, New Telecom Center, No. 7 Guangdong Road, Kowloon Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Lu Bo, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Sun Geng, lawyer of Gansu Dehe Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Suzhou Industrial Park Haifu Investment Co., Ltd. Domicile: B-216, Qingjian Lake Commercial Plaza, No. 9 Xingcheng Road, Weiting Town, Suzhou Industrial Park, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Zhang Yibin, Executive Director of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Ji Jingyi, lawyer of Beijing Fada Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Tu Haitao, lawyer of Beijing Fada Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance: Lu Bo, female, Han ethnicity, born on January 24, 1963, domiciled in Yangpu District, Shanghai, currently residing in Anding District, Dingxi City, Gansu Province.
Agent ad litem: Sun Geng, lawyer of Gansu Dehe Law Firm.

The applicants for retrial, Gansu Shiheng Nonferrous Resources Reuse Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shiheng Company) and Hong Kong Diya Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Diya Company), in the case of dispute over capital increase with the respondent Suzhou Industrial Park Haifu Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haifu Company) and Lu Bo, not satisfied with the civil judgment (2011) Gan Min Er Zhong Zi No. 96 rendered by the Gansu High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2011) Min Shen Zi No. 1522, decided to initiate a retrial of this case and, in accordance with the law, formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing on April 10, 2012. Sun Geng, agent ad litem for Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo, and Ji Jingyi, agent ad litem for Haifu Company, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

On December 30, 2009, Haifu Company filed a lawsuit with the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo to pay it the agreed compensation of RMB 19,982,095 and to bear the litigation costs and other expenses of this case.

The Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court of Gansu Province found the following facts at first instance: Prior to November 1, 2007, Gansu Zhongxing Zinc Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongxing Company), Haifu Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo jointly entered into a "Capital Increase Agreement of Gansu Zhongxing Zinc Industry Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Capital Increase Agreement"), which stipulates: The registered capital of Zhongxing Company is USD 3.84 million, with Diya Company holding 100% of the investment. The parties agree that Haifu Company will make a cash capital contribution of RMB 20 million to Zhongxing Company, accounting for 3.85% of the registered capital after the capital increase, and Diya Company will account for 96.15%. According to the content of the agreement, Diya Company and Haifu Company shall enter into a joint venture contract and amend the articles of association, and within 10 days from the date of approval of the joint venture contract and the amended articles of association, the subscribed capital increase shall be paid in a lump sum into the account designated by Zhongxing Company. The joint venture contract and the amended articles of association shall take effect upon approval by the competent government authorities. When Haifu Company fulfills its capital contribution obligation, Lu Bo undertakes to transfer the Wudu Niugang lead-zinc mine in Ebian County, Sichuan Province, to the name of Zhongxing Company before December 31, 2007. The raised funds shall be mainly used for the following projects: 1. Acquisition of a zinc smelting plant with an annual production capacity of more than 15,000 tons within Gansu Province; 2. Development of the Niugang mine in Ebian County, Sichuan Province; 3. Investment of RMB 5 million in research on cyclic smelting technology. Article 7, special provisions, item 1: After the signing of this agreement, Zhongxing Company shall promptly establish a "Company Restructuring and Listing Working Group" to commence the preparatory work for the company's restructuring and listing, with the working group composed of shareholder representatives and key management personnel. The parties to the agreement shall, when conditions are met, restructure the company into a standard joint stock limited company and strive for an initial public offering on a domestic stock exchange. Item 2, performance target stipulation: The net profit of Zhongxing Company for 2008 shall not be less than RMB 30 million. If the actual net profit of Zhongxing Company for 2008 fails to reach RMB 30 million, Haifu Company shall have the right to demand compensation from Zhongxing Company; if Zhongxing Company fails to fulfill the compensation obligation, Haifu Company shall have the right to demand that Diya Company fulfill the compensation obligation. Compensation amount = (1 - Actual net profit for 2008 / RMB 30 million) x Amount of this investment. Item 4, equity repurchase stipulation: If, by October 20, 2010, due to reasons attributable to Zhongxing Company, the listing cannot be completed, Haifu Company shall have the right to demand at any time that Diya Company repurchase all of the equity in Zhongxing Company then held by Haifu Company. Diya Company shall, within 180 days from the date of receipt of the written notice from Haifu Company, pay the full repurchase price in a lump sum to Haifu Company according to the following terms: If from January 1, 2008, the annualized return on net assets of Zhongxing Company exceeds 10%, then the repurchase amount payable by Diya Company shall be the book value of the owner's equity corresponding to the shares of Zhongxing Company held by Haifu Company; if from January 1, 2008, the annualized return on net assets of Zhongxing Company is lower than 10%, then the repurchase amount payable by Diya Company shall be (Original investment amount of Haifu Company - Compensation amount) x (1 + 10% x Number of investment days / 360). In addition, the agreement also stipulates information disclosure obligations, liability for breach of contract, etc., and provides that this agreement shall take effect from the date of signing indicated at the beginning of the agreement upon being signed by authorized representatives and affixed with official seals. Matters not provided for or not clearly agreed upon in this agreement shall be handled by reference to the amended articles of association of Zhongxing Company and the investment contract between the shareholders (if any).

On November 1, 2007, Haifu Company and Diya Company signed the "Contract for Sino- Foreign Equity Joint Venture Gansu Zhongxing Zinc Industry Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Joint Venture Contract"), with the following relevant provisions: Zhongxing Company will increase its capital and expand its shares to raise the registered capital to USD 3.9938 million; Haifu Company decides to acquire part of the equity, changing Zhongxing Company from a foreign-invested enterprise to a Sino-foreign equity joint venture. In the section on the establishment of the joint venture, it is stipulated that each party to the joint venture shall be liable to the joint venture company to the extent of its subscribed capital contribution or the joint venture conditions it provides. Haifu Company contributes USD 153,800, accounting for 3.85% of the registered capital; Diya Company contributes USD 3.84 million, accounting for 96.15% of the registered capital. Haifu Company shall pay RMB 20 million in a lump sum to the joint venture company within 10 days after this contract becomes effective; the portion exceeding its subscribed registered capital in the joint venture company shall be recorded as capital reserve of the joint venture company. Articles 68 and 69, regarding the profit distribution of the joint venture company, stipulate: The profits of the joint venture company after payment of income tax and allocation of various funds shall be distributed according to the shareholding ratio of each joint venture party. No profit shall be distributed before losses of the previous fiscal year of the joint venture company are made up. Undistributed profits of the previous fiscal year may be included in the profit distribution of the current fiscal year. The term, dissolution, and liquidation of the joint venture company are also stipulated. It also specially provides: After the completion of the change of the joint venture company, a "Company Restructuring and Listing Working Group" shall be promptly established to commence the preparatory work for the company's restructuring and listing, with the working group composed of shareholder representatives and key management personnel. The joint venture company shall, when conditions are met, be restructured into a joint stock limited company and strive for an initial public offering on a domestic stock exchange. If, by October 20, 2010, due to reasons attributable to the joint venture company itself, the listing cannot be completed, Haifu Company shall have the right to demand at any time that Diya Company repurchase all of the equity in the joint venture company then held by Haifu Company. This contract shall take effect upon approval by the approval authority. The "Articles of Association of Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Gansu Zhongxing Zinc Industry Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Articles of Association"), Articles 62 and 63, contain the same content as Articles 68 and 69 of the Joint Venture Contract. Thereafter, Haifu Company, as agreed, deposited RMB 20 million into Zhongxing Company's bank account on November 2, 2007, of which RMB 1,147,717 was attributed to the increase in registered capital and RMB 18,852,283 was attributed to capital reserve. On February 29, 2008, the Gansu Provincial Department of Commerce, by document Gan Shang Wai Zi Zi [2008] No. 79, "Reply on the Capital Increase and Equity Change of Gansu Zhongxing Zinc Industry Co., Ltd.," approved the capital increase and equity change, and approved "the capital increase agreement, joint venture contract, and articles of association signed by both parties on November 1, 2007, shall take effect from the date hereof." Subsequently, Zhongxing Company handled the corresponding industrial and commercial registration changes based on this approval. In June 2009, Zhongxing Company handled the corresponding industrial and commercial registration changes based on this approval. In June 2009, with approval from the Gansu Provincial Department of Commerce, Zhongxing Company went through the registration procedures for change of name and business scope with the industry and commerce department, and its name was changed to Gansu Shiheng Nonferrous Resources Reuse Co., Ltd. According to the industrial and commercial annual inspection report records, the total operating profit of Zhongxing Company for the fiscal year 2008 was RMB 26,858.13, and the net profit was RMB 26,858.13.

The court of first instance held that, based on the arguments of both parties, the issues in dispute in the case were: 1. Whether the content of Article 7, Item (2) of the Capital Increase Agreement has legal effect; 2. If valid, whether Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo should bear compensation liability.

Upon review, the Capital Increase Agreement represented the true intent of both parties. However, the content of Article 7, Item (2), namely, the stipulation that if the actual net profit of Shiheng Company for 2008 fails to reach RMB 30 million, Haifu Company has the right to demand compensation from Shiheng Company, did not comply with the provisions of Article 8 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures, which requires that enterprise profits be distributed according to the proportion of registered capital contributed by each joint venture party. At the same time, this provision was inconsistent with the relevant clauses of the Articles of Association and also harmed the interests of the company and its creditors, and did not comply with the provisions of Article 20, Paragraph 1 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, pursuant to Article 52, Item (5) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the provision that Shiheng Company bears compensation liability to Haifu Company violated mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations and was invalid. Accordingly, Haifu Company's claim for compensation from Shiheng Company based on this clause could not be supported by law. Since the provision requiring Shiheng Company to bear compensation liability was invalid, Haifu Company's claim for compensation from Shiheng Company lost its prerequisite basis. Meanwhile, the content of Article 7, Item (2) of the Capital Increase Agreement was inconsistent with the relevant provisions in the Joint Venture Contract. Pursuant to Article 10, Paragraph 2 of the Implementing Regulations for the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures, the content of the Joint Venture Contract shall prevail. Therefore, Haifu Company's basis for demanding compensation from Diya Company was insufficient and was not supported by law. Although Lu Bo was the legal representative of Shiheng Company, her actions in Shiheng Company represented the company's conduct and interests, and the content of Article 7, Item (2) of the Capital Increase Agreement did not contain any provision regarding Lu Bo's personal obligation to pay compensation. Therefore, Haifu Company's claim for Lu Bo to bear personal compensation liability lacked both contractual and legal basis and should be dismissed by law. As for the fact that Lu Bo failed to transfer the Wudu Niugang lead-zinc mine in Ebian County, Sichuan Province, to the name of Shiheng Company before December 31, 2007, as promised, this involved a breach of duty towards Shiheng Company and its shareholders and could not serve as a reason for Lu Bo to bear compensation liability in this case.

In summary, the court of first instance held that Haifu Company's claims could not be supported by law, and the defense arguments of Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo that they should not bear compensation liability were valid. Pursuant to Article 52, Item (5) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 6, Paragraph 2, and Article 20, Paragraph 1 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 2, Paragraphs 1 and 2, and Article 3 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures, and Article 10, Paragraph 2 of the Implementing Regulations for the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures, the court rendered the civil judgment (2010) Lan Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 71 on December 31, 2010, dismissing all of Haifu Company's claims.

Haifu Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Gansu High People's Court.

The facts found at second instance were consistent with those at first instance.

The court of second instance held: The focus of the dispute between the parties was whether Article 7, Item (2) of the Capital Increase Agreement had legal effect. In this case, although the agreement signed by the four parties, Haifu Company, Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo, was titled "Capital Increase Agreement," a review of the entire content of the agreement revealed that Haifu Company's purpose in paying RMB 20 million was not merely to hold 3.85% of the equity in Shiheng Company (amounting to USD 153,800, equivalent to RMB 1,147,710). Rather, the core purpose of entering into the agreement and making the capital contribution was to obtain the increased value of the equity after Shiheng Company underwent a joint-stock reform and successfully listed. Based on this investment purpose, the four parties, including Haifu Company, agreed on a performance target in Article 7, Item (2) of the Capital Increase Agreement, namely: "The net profit of Shiheng Company for 2008 shall not be less than RMB 30 million. Haifu Company has the right to demand compensation from Shiheng Company; if Shiheng Company fails to fulfill the compensation obligation, Haifu Company has the right to demand that Diya Company fulfill the compensation obligation. Compensation amount = (1 - Actual net profit for 2008 / RMB 30 million) x Amount of this investment." The agreement among the four parties that Shiheng Company's net profit for 2008 should not be less than RMB 30 million was merely a requirement regarding the target enterprise's profitability and did not involve specific distribution matters; moreover, if the profit target was achieved, Shiheng Company and its shareholders could each obtain their corresponding benefits in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the Joint Venture Contract, the Articles of Association, and other relevant provisions, which would also help protect the interests of creditors. Therefore, this provision did not violate the law. However, the agreement among the four parties that if the actual net profit of Shiheng Company for 2008 failed to reach RMB 30 million, Haifu Company had the right to demand compensation from Shiheng Company and Diya Company in a certain manner, violated the principle of risk-sharing in the investment field, enabling Haifu Company, as an investor, to obtain agreed returns without bearing any risk, regardless of Shiheng Company's business performance. By reference to Article 4, Item 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Joint Operation Contract Disputes," which provides: "Where an enterprise legal person or institutional legal person invests in a joint operation entity as a joint operation party but does not participate in joint management and does not bear the risks of the joint operation, and recovers the principal and interest or collects fixed profits on a regular basis regardless of profit or loss, it is a joint operation in name but a loan in substance, violating relevant financial regulations, and the contract should be held invalid," the relevant content of Article 7, Item (2) of the Capital Increase Agreement should be held invalid for violating Article 52, Item (5) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. Apart from the RMB 1,147,710 that had been included in Shiheng Company's registered capital, the remaining RMB 18,852,283 should be characterized in substance as a loan under the guise of an investment. Although the compensation commitments of Shiheng Company and Diya Company were also invalid, Haifu Company entered into the contract based on reasonable reliance on those commitments; therefore, Shiheng Company and Diya Company should bear primary fault liability for the legal consequences of the invalidity. Pursuant to Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Shiheng Company and Diya Company should jointly return the RMB 18,852,283 to Haifu Company, along with interest for the period of possession. Since Haifu Company also bore some fault for the legal consequences of the invalidity, paying interest at the benchmark bank loan rate for the same period would not reflect its share of fault liability. Therefore, Shiheng Company and Diya Company should pay interest at the bank fixed deposit rate for the same period.

Since Lu Bo, as an individual, did not make any commitment to Haifu Company regarding the compensation issue under Article 7, Item (2) of the Capital Increase Agreement, and whether she transferred the Wudu Niugang lead-zinc mine in Ebian County, Sichuan Province, to the name of Shiheng Company before December 31, 2007, does not pertain to the same legal relationship as this case, Haifu Company's claim for Lu Bo to bear compensation liability lacked both factual and legal basis and was not supported by law.

Regarding the argument raised by Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo in their defense that the Capital Increase Agreement had been superseded by the Joint Venture Contract subsequently signed between Haifu Company and Diya Company, and that Article 7(2) of the Capital Increase Agreement no longer had legally binding force on the parties. Because the Capital Increase Agreement and the Joint Venture Contract had different contracting parties, the rights and obligations stipulated therein were inconsistent, and on February 29, 2008, the Reply of the Gansu Provincial Department of Commerce, Document No. Ganshang Waizi Zi [2008] 79, titled "Reply on the Capital Increase and Equity Change of Gansu Zhongxing Zinc Industry Co., Ltd.," expressly stated in the second paragraph: "The capital increase agreement, joint venture contract, and articles of association signed by the two investing parties on November 1, 2001, shall take effect from the date hereof." Therefore, their defense was not sustained. The court of first instance held that the judgment of first instance had unclear findings of facts in certain parts, leading to improper application of law in some respects, which should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 153, Items (2) and (3), and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. The civil judgment (2010) Lan Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 71 of the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court was set aside; 2. Shiheng Company and Diya Company were ordered to jointly return RMB 18,852,283 and interest (calculated at the benchmark fixed deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period from November 3, 2007, to the date of full payment) to Haifu Company within 30 days after the judgment took effect.

Shiheng Company and Diya Company, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2011) Gan Min Er Zhong Zi No. 96 of the Gansu High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial, requesting an order for retrial, revocation of the second-instance judgment, and affirmation of the first-instance judgment. The grounds were: 1. Haifu Company's claim in the lawsuit sought payment of profit compensation of RMB 19,982,095 from Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo, and did not request the return of the RMB 18,852,283 that had been credited to the joint venture's capital reserve and its interest. Therefore, the second-instance judgment ordering Shiheng Company and Diya Company to jointly return RMB 18,852,283 and interest exceeded Haifu Company's claims and appellate requests, violating procedural rules. Moreover, the amount of RMB 18,852,283 plus interest exceeded RMB 22 million, clearly exceeding the subject matter of the claim. 2. The second-instance judgment's characterization of the RMB 18,852,283 paid by Haifu Company and credited to the joint venture's capital reserve as "investment in name but loan in substance" was unsupported by evidence and violated legal provisions. 3. The second-instance judgment erroneously applied the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Joint Operation Contracts," as there was no joint operation relationship between Haifu Company and Diya Company or Shiheng Company. 4. Article 97 of the Joint Venture Contract stipulated that the contract superseded any prior oral or written agreements, contracts, representations, and understandings made between the parties regarding the above transactions. Therefore, the Capital Increase Agreement no longer bound the parties. Diya Company had not received any payment under Article 7.2 of the Capital Increase Agreement or the Joint Venture Contract, so ordering Diya Company to bear joint liability for returning the principal and interest had no factual basis.

Haifu Company responded: 1. The Capital Increase Agreement was a comprehensive financing and shareholding reform agreement entered into by four parties for the purpose of an IPO, which could not be subsumed by the Joint Venture Contract. 2. The second-instance court ordered Shiheng Company and Diya Company to return the premium payment that was intended for a specific purpose above the capital contribution, which did not involve the issue of capital withdrawal. 3. In the Capital Increase Agreement, Lu Bo represented only himself, and his conduct was a personal act of a contracting party; he should bear compensation liability for violating the agreement. 4. Lu Bo's conduct was suspected of constituting a criminal offense, as he used false registered capital to mislead Haifu Company into relying on his company's financial strength and defrauded Haifu Company of funds. Haifu Company requested the court to investigate and obtain evidence to ascertain the facts or to refer the case to the public security authorities for investigation.

The facts found upon review by this Court are consistent with those found by the courts of first and second instance.

This Court holds: In December 2009, when Haifu Company initiated the lawsuit before the court of first instance, its claims were to order Shiheng Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo to pay the agreed compensation amount of RMB 19,982,095 to Haifu Company and to bear the litigation costs and other expenses of the case. It did not request the return of the investment amount. Therefore, the second-instance judgment ordering Shiheng Company and Diya Company to jointly return the investment amount and interest exceeded Haifu Company's claims and was erroneous.

As an enterprise legal person, Haifu Company invested in Shiheng Company and then engaged in a joint venture with Diya Company, making Shiheng Company the joint venture enterprise. In the Capital Increase Agreement, Shiheng Company, Haifu Company, Diya Company, and Lu Bo agreed that if Shiheng Company's actual net profit was less than RMB 30 million, Haifu Company would be entitled to compensation from Shiheng Company, and a calculation formula was stipulated. This arrangement allowed Haifu Company to obtain a relatively fixed return on its investment, which was detached from Shiheng Company's operating performance and harmed the interests of the company and its creditors. The courts of first and second instance correctly found that this part of the Capital Increase Agreement was invalid under Article 20 of the Company Law of the PRC and Article 8 of the Law of the PRC on Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures. However, the second-instance court's characterization of Haifu Company's investment of RMB 18,852,283 as a "joint operation in name but a loan in substance" and its order for Shiheng Company and Diya Company to return that investment to Haifu Company lacked legal basis. This Court hereby corrects that error.

The Capital Increase Agreement contained no provision for Lu Bo to compensate Haifu Company, and Haifu Company's request for compensation from Lu Bo lacked contractual basis. Furthermore, Haifu Company's allegation that Lu Bo was suspected of committing a criminal offense was unsupported by evidence. This Court does not sustain that claim either.

However, in the Capital Increase Agreement, Diya Company's commitment to compensate Haifu Company did not harm the interests of the company or its creditors, did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations, represented the true intent of the parties, and was valid. Diya Company promised Haifu Company a net profit target for Zhongxing Company for 2008 and agreed on a method for calculating the compensation amount. Given that Zhongxing Company's profit for 2008 fell short of the agreed target, Diya Company should compensate Haifu Company in accordance with the agreement upon Haifu Company's request. Diya Company did not raise any objection to the compensation amount or the calculation method requested by Haifu Company, and this Court confirms it.

Based on Haifu Company's claims and the fact that certain provisions of the Capital Increase Agreement in this case are invalid, this Court, pursuant to Article 60 of the Contract Law of the PRC, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item 2, and Article 186 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, renders the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2011) Gan Min Er Zhong Zi No. 96 of the Gansu High People's Court is set aside;
2. Within 30 days after this judgment takes effect, Diya Company shall pay Haifu Company the agreed compensation amount of RMB 19,982,095. If Diya Company fails to perform the payment obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC;
3. Haifu Company's other claims are dismissed.

The court costs of first instance of RMB 155,612.3, property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, court mailing fee of RMB 700, and court costs of second instance of RMB 155,612.3, totaling RMB 316,924.6, shall be borne by Diya Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Lu Xiaolong
Judge: Yang Xingye

November 7, 2012
